newsitem.title: USA: Boyd trims staff at Kansas City casino.
newsitem.headline: Boyd trims staff at Kansas City casino.

text.p: Boyd Gaming Corp on Thursday said 39 middle managers lost their jobs at its Sam's Town casino in Kansas City as the company handed over operational duties to a six-member employee executive council.
The move was designed to streamline decision-making and improve customer service at the casino, Rob Stillwell, a spokesman for Las Vegas-based Boyd Gaming, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said reducing expenses was not the main reason for the layoffs, though he acknowledged that the move would help the casino's bottom line.
"This was a customer-service move rather than an expense-related move, although that is certainly an underlying benefit," Stillwell said.
He said streamlined decision-making at the casino would allow front-line employees to sharpen their focus on customer service. He declined to elaborate.
Stillwell said it was too early to estimate the cost savings that might result from the layoffs.

Since Sam's Town opened in September 1995, its workforce has shrunk to about 700 from an initial 1,200 employees, the spokesman said. He attributed the reduction in part to increasing competition in the Kansas City casino market.
Two new casinos have opened there in the last two months, bringing the total number of casinos in the area to five.
Stillwell would not comment about Sam's Town revenues since Station Casinos Inc opened the fourth-largest casino in the United States in Kansas City last month.
Stillwell said traffic at Sam's Town had actually risen since Station opened, but he did not provide specific figures.
Station has attracted large crowds in its first few weeks of operation.
Jay Sevigny, general manager Harrah's North Kansas City Casino & Hotel, owned by Harrah's Entertainment, recently said revenues at his casino were down by about 10 percent since Station opened.
